findings.claim: Natural-gas futures volatility rises materially on storage-report announcement days and is also seasonally elevated in winter.
findings.expected_direction: announcement day and winter -> higher volatility

findings.claim: Natural-gas volatility is not adequately described as a single stationary process; maturity, season, storage state, temperature deviations and announcement timing materially condition it.
findings.expected_direction: conditional-state model should outperform unconditional interpretation

findings.claim: Weather and extreme-weather information can improve out-of-sample natural-gas volatility forecasts relative to otherwise similar volatility models without weather inputs.
findings.expected_direction: weather-conditioned volatility model -> lower forecast loss than unconditioned comparator in relevant regimes
findings.caveat: External OOS evidence supports structured volatility; this programme must reproduce the phenomenon independently.
